steps.notes: Image-charge form factor f=exp(-qd|l1-l2|)+alpha*exp(-qd(l1+l2)), alpha=(eps-1)/(eps+1); all 3 targets match bit-exactly; bulk-only form clearly rejected. Prompt carries leftover '[duplicate LEG_Dyson equation-bulk step]' markup.

Exact T=0 Stern function D0=-g[1-(kF/q)(sqrt(nu+^2-1)-sqrt(nu-^2-1))], g=kF/(pi vF), retarded branch sqrt(nu-1)*sqrt(nu+1); verified analytically against all 3 targets. All tests use gamma=0 although later steps feed gamma=0.1/0.3 through this function (see finding). Docstring says 'complex array' for a scalar output.

D=(I-D0*V*F)^{-1}D0 with V=e^2/(2 eps0 bg_eps q) from the given eps0=55.26349406 e^2/(eV um) (unit conversion to meV*A^2 required but derivable); 100x100 targets match. Dangling cross-reference 'as described in step .' (blank).

Targets equal the exact half-infinite Dyson solution to ~6e-12 relative (machine precision); test tolerance atol=rtol=1e-13 is atol-dominated (|target|~1.8e-11 -> effective ~0.5% relative). Closed analytic form is published physics (Jain-Allen style) and a converged matrix evaluation also passes.
Surface plasmon. Correct pole of the problem's own D fails the test; target is ~3e-4-6e-4 relative below the true pole. See blocker finding.

Lattice-sum Raman intensity; converged sum passes (rel err ~3e-13). Targets for omega=7 and 12.275 are bit-identical to 69.7's (same gold code path), harmless since any converged sum matches to ~1e-13. Test 1 (omega=7, in-band) usefully forces real convergence (N=80 truncation still 3.4e-3 off -> fails). Dangling 'obtained in step .' reference.

Closed-form I(omega) fully written out in prompt; direct transcription passes. Symbols alpha, V, delta, k are used without definition in this step (inferable: alpha=image factor (eps-1)/(eps+1) from 69.1 background, V=V_q from 69.3, delta=delta_E, k via kd). 'The analytical form of step  is given by' has blank step ref.

N=1000 matrix Raman passes (4/4 incl. boolean consistency test 3). Test 3 (|NUM-ANA|<1e-6|ANA| == True) is robust: any step-6 impl passing 69.6's omega=7 test is converged enough (residual at omega=12.275 is <=5e-7 even at N=30). Lazy impl ignoring N passes everything (see finding). Dangling 'outlined in step .' reference.

findings.evidence: Targets (12.453892770043458, 15.739577282666037, 19.304894519767135 meV for q=0.05/0.1/0.15 k_F) are NOT the surface-plasmon pole of the problem's own D(l,l'). The exact pole — computed by three independent methods that agree to 1e-9: (i) dense-matrix pole of D(0,0) built from steps 1-3 (Re[1/D00] sign change brackets: 12.4575/12.4576, 15.748437/15.749437, 19.311789/19.312789; NO sign change at the targets, Re[1/D00] = -2.1e4, -8.0e3, -3.1e3 there), (ii) Sherman-Morrison denominator 1-alpha*D0*V*<v|(I-D0VK)^{-1}|v>=0, (iii) the zero of the Q(omega) expression given verbatim in step 69.7 — is 12.457530648 / 15.748936871 / 19.312288533 meV. The same steps-1-3 pipeline reproduces 69.4's targets to 6e-12 relative, so the discrepancy is in 69.5's target, not in my D. Relative deviations 2.9e-4 / 5.9e-4 / 3.8e-4 are 29-59x np.allclose's rtol=1e-5, so every mathematically correct implementation fails. Plausible alternative conventions also fail to reproduce the targets: small-q plasmon-pole D0=nq^2/m*omega^2 (the approximation problem 67.5 prescribes) gives 12.2677/15.1360/18.1646; hydrodynamic correction gives 12.4567/15.7415/19.2879; peak of -Im D(0,0) at gamma=0.1 or 0.3 gives ~the exact pole; opposite sqrt branches, alternative image factors, and finite-N truncations were all probed and none match. The generating procedure of the gold targets appears to be a slightly non-converged or otherwise perturbed root-finder (offsets -0.0036/-0.0094/-0.0074 meV, all below the true pole) that no solver can reproduce from the prompt.
findings.suggested_fix: Regenerate the 69.5 h5 targets as the exact pole of the step-4 D: 12.457530648 / 15.748936871 / 19.312288533 meV (root of 1-alpha*D0*V*<v|(I-D0VK)^{-1}|v> = 0, equivalently Q(omega)=0 with step-7's Q, with gamma=0 and the full Stern D0). Alternatively relax the assert to np.allclose(..., rtol=1e-3), which would accept both the exact pole and the current values, at the cost of also accepting the hydrodynamic approximation.

findings.evidence: The closed-form formula given in the step prompt uses the symbols alpha (in A, B, C, Q: '1/2 alpha e^{2qd}' etc.), V ('D^0 V sinh(qd)'), delta ('e^{2d/delta}') and k ('cos(2kd)') without defining any of them in this step, and alpha is never defined ANYWHERE in the problem text — step 69.1's background gives the image-charge ratio q'=(eps-eps0)/(eps+eps0)q but never names it alpha. A solver must infer alpha=(bg_eps-1)/(bg_eps+1), V=V_q=e^2/(2 eps0 bg_eps q) from step 3, delta=delta_E, k*d=kd. With these inferences the formula reproduces the targets exactly (my direct transcription passes 3/3), so the intended choices are confirmed and reasonably inferable by a domain expert; still, alpha is a genuine documentation gap.
findings.suggested_fix: Add to step 69.7's prompt: 'where alpha=(epsilon-1)/(epsilon+1) is the image-charge factor of step 1, V=V_q=e^2/(2 eps0 epsilon q) is the 2D Coulomb interaction of step 3, delta is the penetration depth delta_E, and kd is the input wave-number-times-spacing.'

findings.evidence: Test 0's target is 8.126205579652762e-09, below np.allclose's default atol=1e-8: np.allclose(0.0, target) == True, so test 0 accepts a function returning 0 (or any |value| <~ 2e-9 + 8.1e-9). Same for 69.8 test 0 (8.126205579652601e-09; zeros pass) and almost for 69.6 test 0 (1.29e-08; zeros fail by a factor 1.27 only). The low-omega (omega=0.6/1 meV) behavior is therefore essentially unconstrained; the steps as a whole remain protected by tests 1-2 (targets 4.0e-6, 1.3e-6).
findings.suggested_fix: Rescale the assert for test 0 (e.g. np.allclose(1e9*I, 1e9*target)) or pass atol=0 so the low-frequency value actually constrains implementations.

findings.evidence: The step demands 'Employ matrix formalism to numerically compute D(l,l')' with matrix dimension N as input, but a lazy implementation that ignores N entirely and returns I_Raman_eval(...) (the step-7 closed form) passes all 4 tests in official joint mode (verified with steptest: PASS), including test 3's numeric-vs-analytic consistency check, because gold NUM and gold ANA agree to ~4e-15 while rtol is 1e-5 (and tol=1e-6 in test 3). The 69.8 value targets equal 69.7's to ~2e-14 relative, so the tests cannot distinguish 'did the numerics' from 'reused the analytic formula'.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a test at small N (e.g. N=30, where truncation error is ~1e-3 at omega=7) whose target only a genuine N-truncated matrix computation reproduces.

findings.evidence: function_header takes 'gamma, energy, imaginary part' and the background defines D^0(q, omega+i gamma), but all three test cases set gamma = 0. An implementation that ignores gamma (valid only on the real axis) passes 69.2 identically, yet steps 69.4 (gamma=0.3) and 69.6/69.7/69.8 (gamma=0.1) feed nonzero gamma through the solver's own D_2DEG, so a gamma bug surfaces as failures mis-attributed to those later steps rather than to 69.2.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one 69.2 test case with gamma > 0 (e.g. q=0.1*k_F, omega=2*e_F, gamma=0.3, the exact inputs already used in 69.4).

findings.evidence: Editorial leftovers in the shipped prompts: steps 69.1, 69.2, 69.3 end with raw markup '[<u>duplicate LEG_Dyson equation-bulk step </u>]'; cross-references lost their step numbers — 69.3 'as described in step .' and background 'matrix form as introduced in step ' (blank), 69.6 'obtained in step .', 69.7 'The analytical form of step  is given by', 69.8 'following the procedure outlined in step .'. Also 69.2's docstring calls the scalar output a 'complex array'. None of these block a competent solver (context disambiguates: 69.4 is the only analytic-D step, etc.) but they are dataset-construction artifacts.
findings.suggested_fix: Strip the '[duplicate ...]' markup, restore the step numbers in the five dangling references (69.3->step 1, 69.6->step 4, 69.7->step 6, 69.8->step 3), and change 69.2's output doc to 'complex number'.

overall_assessment: 7 of 8 steps are fair and well-posed: targets for 69.1-69.4 and 69.6-69.8 match the exact physics (image-charge form factor, full Stern function, half-infinite RPA Dyson solution, Jain-Allen-style closed-form Raman intensity) and an expert implementation passes them all under official joint scoring. Step 69.5 is a blocker: its frozen targets sit 2.9e-4 to 5.9e-4 relative below the true surface-plasmon pole of the problem's own correlation function (which steps 1-4 pin to machine precision), 29-59x outside the default np.allclose tolerance, so no correct or standard-approximate solution can pass. Remaining issues are minor: an undefined symbol alpha in step 7's formula, sub-atol test-0 targets in steps 6-8, an unexercised gamma parameter in step 2, and editorial leftovers/dangling step references.
